Subject: Potential data exfiltration affecting subset of tenants

Sofia / Marissa —

We need to flag a potential security event that may affect a small subset of MapleBank customers. Our SOC saw anomalous outbound traffic from an integration key used to pull embeddings last night (approx 02:40 UTC). At this stage we cannot conclude exfiltration of sensitive customer PII, but the pattern looks like repeated bulk pulls.

Per our DPA (Section 9), we are escalating to request:
- Initial confirmation of whether Redwood observed any suspicious outbound transfer tied to the MapleBank tenant ID (MB-78A) within the timeframe below.
- A copy of logs relevant to the tenant, including access logs and subprocessor API calls for the 30–60 minute window around the anomaly.
- Contact for escalation / evidence handover.

Timeline: we need an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours, and preliminary evidence (logs/exports) within 72 hours to meet internal review windows.

We appreciate this is sensitive; please let us know the best path for secure evidence transfer (SFTP, pre-signed object, or secure Drive with audit).

Thanks,
James O'Neill
Senior Incident Responder
MapleBank Security

----------

Hi James — thanks for the heads-up and the detail. We take these reports seriously. Quick read-through and next steps below.

Acknowledgement: We acknowledge receipt and will treat this as an incident while we investigate.

Clarifying Qs:
- Can you confirm the tenant ID(s) you believe are impacted (you mentioned MB-78A; any others)?
- Any indicator of compromise (file hashes, IPs, object keys) you can share now will speed triage.

Proposed Redwood response plan (subject to confirmation):
- Initial acknowledgement: within 6 hours (we can confirm triage owner and ETA).
- Preliminary log pull: within 72 hours after we receive the tenant IDs and scope. This will include access logs, API call records to subprocessor endpoints, and KV cache churn metrics.
- For confirmed incidents we propose a follow-up evidence handover window of 7 business days (to allow for cross-team collection and redaction) — we can expedite if you need raw exports sooner.

Subprocessors & transfers:
- We'll provide a mapping of active subprocessors for MB-78A and note any cross-border egress. If SCCs or other transfer mechanisms are needed for EU->US material, we will flag that explicitly and coordinate the minimal export package.

Secure handover: we prefer an SFTP endpoint with short-lived credentials or a secure SharePoint/Drive link with audit. Please confirm which you prefer.

I am looping in Marissa (customer ops) and Vivek (privacy/infra) to coordinate the DPA redline implications and evidence preservation. Attaching a short checklist of what we'll prioritize.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 15:28:00 +00:00
Subject: Internal: DPA incident clause — proposed compromise language

Team —

I pulled the contract (MapleBank DPA v2) and the notification clause reads quite aggressively (48-hour initial notice for any suspected incident). Given our operational footprint and the need to avoid false positives moving to customers, I suggest pushing for the following compromise redline:

- Initial notification: "Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a reported or detected event affecting a customer's tenant within 24 hours of becoming aware, and will provide an assessment of impact (confirmed/unconfirmed) within 72 hours."
- Evidence handover: "For incidents confirmed to materially affect the customer, Redwood will deliver relevant logs and forensics exports within 7 business days unless a shorter timeline is mutually agreed in writing; Redwood will prioritize exports if law/regulation requires faster transfer."
- Subprocessor access: "Redwood will disclose which subprocessors processed the affected tenant's data in the 30-day window around the incident and will coordinate evidence collection from those subprocessors subject to customer NDA/transfer rules."

Operational notes: we can meet the 24/72 construct operationally if Maple provides tenant IDs and a secure transfer endpoint immediately. For the 7-day evidence window, we may need legal carve-outs for redaction and for gathering subprocessor logs (some vendors require 48–72h).

I've drafted suggested redline text and attached. Priyom, can you advise if we need a clause referencing SCCs or specific data transfer mechanisms for EU customers? Vivek — please confirm whether we can produce the API/subprocessor logs in the requested form and whether we need an emergency-access escalation path.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-dpa-redlines.docx

- Impacted tenant list: MB-78A and MB-79C.
- Indicators: outbound to 54.83.12.97 and object key pattern "maple-export-*".
- Timeline constraints: internal audit requires preliminary evidence within 72 hours; final forensic exports within 5 business days if possible.

On SCCs/data transfers: our legal team says explicit mention of SCCs in the DPA is preferred for cross-border exports; if Redwood intends to rely on SCCs, please confirm.

We appreciate your cooperation. If we can get the acknowledgement and a named Redwood triage owner within 6 hours, we will treat the 72-hour window as met.

Regards,
James

James / MapleBank legal —

Thanks for the indicators and for confirming tenant IDs. We have triage owner assigned: Vivek Kulkarni (vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com). Our agreement points and actions below — please consider this an operational acknowledgement as well as a proposed set of contract redlines for immediate review.

Operational ack & timeline:
- Acknowledgement: delivered (Sofia) at 2028-11-03T11:05Z.
- Triage owner & point-of-contact: Vivek Kulkarni (cc'd). Vivek will post initial status updates to the secure SFTP channel.
- Preliminary evidence pull: Redwood will prioritize API/access logs for MB-78A and MB-79C and will provide a preliminary packet within 72 hours of confirmed scope receipt (target: 2028-11-06T11:00Z).
- For confirmed incidents we will target forensic exports within 5 business days; if subprocessors are involved this may require an additional 48–72 hours due to vendor SLAs.

Contractual redlines (proposal):
- Notice timing: "Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a reported or detected event affecting a customer's tenant within 24 hours and will provide a preliminary impact assessment within 72 hours of Redwood's confirmation of scope."
- Evidence transfer: "For incidents confirmed to materially affect the customer, Redwood will deliver relevant logs and forensics exports within 5 business days where operationally feasible; Redwood will notify the customer promptly if subprocessors add additional collection time and will use commercially reasonable efforts to expedite."
- Subprocessors: "Redwood will provide a list of subprocessors who processed the customer's data in the 30-day window around the incident and will coordinate evidence collection; Redwood will require a written request and an agreed transfer mechanism for any third-party exports."
- Cross-border transfers: "Where EU personal data must be exported, Redwood will rely on SCCs if applicable and will provide the customer with the transfer legal basis and any related documentation upon request."

Secure handover: please send SFTP host and PGP public key to Vivek at vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com. We will provision short-lived credentials and post checksums and a joint evidence access log to the Drive folder linked below once transfer begins.

Next steps:

2) Redwood to deliver preliminary log packet by 2028-11-06T11:00Z (target).
3) Legal teams to review the proposed redlines; I've attached the redline doc and included a DocuSign link if Maple prefers to sign an interim MOU committing to the transfer timetable.
